translation_rules.style: High-precision Hán-Việt for spells, arrays, and magic tiers, natural Vietnamese flow, keep Western names original in Latin or translate to standard English names if the author used them, rather than Hán-Việt transcription. Eastern and Chinese Han-Viet proper names must remain Hán-Việt.
translation_rules.proper_names_handling: Original names format. Prioritize standard Western names (e.g., Leylin, Robin) instead of transcribing them into Han-Viet (e.g. Lôi Lâm, La Tân) where appropriate. However, any proper names with Eastern, Chinese Han-Viet context must remain Hán-Việt, never Latinized.
forbidden_content: Inline Chinese characters for non-proper names
Latinizing Eastern or Chinese Han-Viet proper names
translation_rules.annotation_style: Add a 'Chú thích' section at the end of the chapter for necessary terms and proper names
translation_rules.honorifics_handling: Translate to appropriate Vietnamese social hierarchy terms, matching a wizard academy and aristocratic hierarchy
translation_rules.technical_terms: Use consistent Vietnamese equivalents from glossary

notes: Truyện bối cảnh Thế giới Vu sư phương Tây, nhân vật chính xuyên không mang theo chíp phân tích AI. Các yếu tố quan trọng: khoa học viễn tưởng kết hợp ma thuật huyền bí, kỵ sĩ xưng hô trang trọng, phép thuật, thí nghiệm di truyền học.

narrator_pronoun_guide: Use standard objective third-person narration style. Match Vietnamese storytelling tradition for the specific context (Western fantasy, aristocracy, etc.). The narrator should use context-appropriate pronouns for characters (e.g., 'hắn', 'anh', or 'chàng' for the male protagonist depending on the tone of the scene - romantic/heroic vs neutral/dark; 'y' for scholars or neutral males; 'lão' or 'ông ta' for old men; 'cô/nàng' for females). Do not rigidly use only one pronoun if the context demands nuance.
